title: Apple Leading The Way Lower On Wall Street - U.S. Commentary
text:
Apple Leading The Way Lower On Wall Street - U.S. Stocks have moved significantly lower in morning trading on Monday, extending the notable downward move seen in the previous session. With the drop, the Dow continues to give back ground after reaching its best closing level in a month last Thursday.
In recent trading, the major averages have seen further downside, hitting new lows for the session. The Dow is down 264.79 points or 1 percent at 25,724.51, the Nasdaq is down 136.23 points or 1.8 percent at 7,270.68 and the S&P 500 is down 27.12 points or 1 percent at 2,753.89.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple ( AAPL ) is weighing on Wall Street, with the tech giant tumbling by 4.7 percent to its lowest intraday level in over three months.
The steep drop by Apple comes after iPhone parts supplier Lumentum cut its fiscal second quarter guidance, adding to recent concerns about iPhone demand.
Concerns also contributing to the weakness on Wall Street.
Light trading activity may be exaggerating the downward momentum, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks are closed in observance of Veterans Day.
A lack of major U.S. economic data on the sidelines ahead of the release of reports on consumer price inflation, retail sales, and industrial production in the coming days.
A speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Wednesday is also likely to attract attention, as traders look for additional clues about the outlook for interest rates.
Last week, the Fed left interest rates unchanged as widely expected but indicated it remains on track to gradually raise rates despite signs of a slowdown in the pace of growth in business investment.
Semiconductor stocks have shown a substantial move to the downside in morning trading, dragging the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down by 3.6 percent.
Within the semiconductor sector, Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) is posting a steep loss after Citi downgraded its rating on the Apple chip supplier's stock to Neutral from Buy.
Considerable weakness has also emerged among tobacco stocks, which are extending the sell-off seen last Friday after a report from the Wall Street Journal said FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb plans to pursue a ban on menthol cigarettes.
Computer hardware, biotechnology, and brokerage stocks are also seeing significant weakness on the day, moving lower along with most of the other major sectors.
In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Monday. Japan'sNikkei 225 Index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index both inched up by 0.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index shot up by 1.2 percent.
Meanwhile, the major European markets have moved to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index has tumbled by 1.4 percent, the French CAC 40 Index and the U.K.'sFTSE 100 Index are down by 0.5 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.
Treasuries moved notably higher during the trading session last Friday, but the bond markets are closed on the day in observance of Veterans Day. //www.rttnews.com/2954292/apple-leading-the-way-lower-on-wall-street-u-s-
